summary: Repo evidence ties the encoder question to ONE documented failure mode: land-trained depth policies fit held-out land data fine (pos RMSE 17-21 mm, yaw corr 0.59-0.83 for all three encoders) but are mostly unresponsive to object bearing underwater. The 2026-09-10/11 E/A/C ablation (ResNet34-BN / ViT-B CLIP / ResNet34-GN, 62 ep, batch 32, 200 ep) showed: (a) the wandb "C wins 4-7x" result was an EMA/BatchNorm artefact; re-measured with `model` weights E is best on held-out; (b) underwater (open-loop replay of 0908 observe runs) the ranking inverts: A (ViT-CLIP) was the only variant that tracked the can, but only in the single L/R-balanced run 173106; in 3 of 4 testable runs ALL variants had r~0, and C always turned right regardless of the can. The repo's own attribution has moved from "yaw head OOD default" (0908) to "data/label geometry" (handheld TCP +4.1 deg label zero, no large-bearing demos -> fixed by the 9/9 recollection) to "land->water transfer of the visual features, scene-shape gap, confounded by old-vs-new can" (0911). Encoder-as-bottleneck is explicitly recorded as a HYPOTHESIS from one run, not a finding. The A checkpoint was flown closed-loop on 2026-09-13 (46 engagements) but only follower speed was analysed; no yaw/encoder verdict exists for that day. Checkpoint convention: `model` weights (not `ema_model`) since 2026-09-07, ranked on the 219/195-window held-out set, last epoch (195) taken. Important corrections to the brief: every actual run used batch 32 (config default 64 was overridden); the observation has NO ImageNet/CLIP mean-std normalisation (obs enters the backbone as [0,1] pseudo-RGB = [inv_depth, validity, inv_depth]); ViT-B trains at ~97 s/epoch vs ResNet34 ~29 s/epoch on the 5090.

facts.fact: E/A/C ablation definition: E = resnet34.a1_in1k pretrained with BatchNorm kept (use_group_norm true but gated off by pretrained), A = vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai, C = resnet34.a1_in1k + force_group_norm true. All: seed 42, batch 32, obs_encoder_lr 3e-5, lr 3e-4 cosine, 200 epochs, use_ema true, frozen false, feature_aggregation null (ViT uses ALL tokens), RandomCrop 0.95 + RandomRotation +/-5 deg, dataset 9_9_26 (62 episodes).

facts.fact: EMA/BatchNorm defect (root cause, confirmed 2026-09-06): EMAModel.step iterates named_parameters() only so BN running_mean/var buffers are never averaged, and transformer_obs_encoder.py gate `use_group_norm and not pretrained` silently skipped the GroupNorm swap because pretrained=true -> the EMA copy's BN stats stayed at timm ImageNet values (num_batches_tracked: timm 374,981 / ckpt ema 374,983 / ckpt model 395,128; max BN buffer relative diff 9847x). Held-out (219 windows, DDIM 16): ema pos RMSE 30.9 mm vs model 20.8 mm (1.82-1.91x); swapping only the 108 BN buffers into the EMA copy recovers 92% of the gap. Fix landed as `force_group_norm` flag (encoder line 71, gate at line 128: `use_group_norm and (force_group_norm or not pretrained)`); the loader in rov_gui/perception/dp_policy.py had to be patched 2026-09-11 to read force_group_norm or C ckpts fail strict load. ViT variants have no BatchNorm2d so the defect cannot arise (EMA ~ model for A).

risks_for_dinov3: The documented failure is land->water TRANSFER of yaw response, not held-out fit: all three encoders already reach 17-21 mm / yaw corr 0.59-0.83 on held-out (consults.md 2026-09-11 line 89). A DINOv3 run judged on held-out MSE or wandb val cannot address the failure; the only discriminating test on record is underwater can-bearing response (rov_gui/tools/policy_yaw_vs_can.py on L/R-balanced observe runs), and even that showed ALL variants unresponsive in 3 of 4 testable runs -- so a null result for DINOv3 would be indistinguishable from the baseline unless new balanced runs with the NEW object are collected first (the old-can vs new-can confound is unresolved).

Held-out and underwater rankings already inverted once (E>A>C vs A>>E>C, memory dp-ablation-groupnorm-wins.md); selecting a DINOv3 checkpoint by the workspace val curve or by held-out alone is documented to pick the wrong model. Any DINOv3 attempt must ship with the underwater replay protocol (policy_session_replay.py + plot_policy_map / policy_yaw_vs_can) and the `--weights model` held-out protocol.

Data scale: 62 episodes / ~16.6k windows [유도]. The 85.8M ViT-B CLIP already overfits 49x (train_action_mse 2e-05 vs val 0.00098, A_vitclip_0910_095251.log) at encoder lr 3e-5 unfrozen. DINOv3-L (303M) / H+ (840M) / 7B are 3.5x / 9.8x / 78x larger; unfrozen full fine-tuning at this data scale is expected to overfit harder [예측]; the repo has no frozen-encoder or LoRA baseline to compare against (training.freeze_encoder: false everywhere).

Compute: ViT-B trained at ~97 s/epoch uncontended (A_vitclip.log epochs 77-79) vs ResNet34 ~29 s/epoch; 200 epochs of ViT-B = ~5.4 h [유도] (actual 9 h 10 min because a duplicate run shared the GPU). DINOv3-L at 201 tokens x 2 frames and ~3.5x params implies >=19 h per 200-epoch run [예측]; H+ and 7B unfrozen with AdamW states (7B: ~13 GB bf16 weights + ~54 GB fp32 Adam moments [유도]) do not fit a single 32 GB RTX 5090 without freezing/8-bit optimisers. The training box also hard-crashed 3x on 2026-09-10 with no auto-restart (memory training-machine-hard-crashes-20260910.md), so multi-day runs carry real loss risk.

Input-statistics mismatch: the obs is [inverse_depth, validity, inverse_depth] in [0,1] with NO mean/std normalisation anywhere in the chain (umi_dataset.py:286; no Normalize in transformer_obs_encoder.py). DINOv3 (and CLIP) pretrained weights expect ImageNet-normalised RGB; the repo has never measured how much of a pretrained encoder's benefit survives this (plan doc line 154-156 assumed 'nearly nil' for CLIP; the A result weakly contradicts it, one run). A DINOv3 study inherits the same un-normalised 3-channel-depth input unless the intake is changed, which would then break parity with existing checkpoints.

Token budget and latency: 'vit' names pass ALL tokens (feature_aggregation null) into the 7-layer/768-d action transformer: DINOv3 ViT at 224 gives 201 tokens x 2 frames = 402 image tokens (vs 98 for ResNet34, 394 for CLIP ViT-B) plus a new Linear(1024/1280/4096 -> 768) projection. Live inference already had to drop DDIM 16 -> 8 because 319 ms inference made 41% of plans late (consults.md 2026-09-02 line 63), and the GPU is shared with FoundationStereo (7.26 Hz, 137 ms solve). A larger encoder directly eats the plan-age budget that the follower deadband analysis identified as a key lever (KNOWN_ISSUES.md lines 281-307: obs age p50 0.5 s already leaves only 0.25-0.4 s of a 3 s horizon weighted).

Environment split: the training env umi2 has timm 0.9.7 with no dinov3 models (established); the deploy env has timm 1.0.29. The parity fixture (parity_20260907.log) is written in the training env and checked in the deploy env, and the C ckpt already failed strict load once because the loader lagged the training-side flag. A DINOv3 attempt needs a timm upgrade in umi2 (numpy/torch pin risk) or a new training env, plus a new parity reference, plus loader changes in rov_gui/perception/dp_policy.py -- all of which the brief says must not be written yet.

Licence/provenance: timm tags the DINOv3 weights 'dinov3-license' (established); the repo's measurement rule requires provenance on every cited number, and there is no memory/journal entry yet on whether the DINOv3 licence terms are acceptable for this project's use.
